subject: English
passage: To investigate the history of coral reef development in ancient oceans, marine biologist Doyin Ezeh and colleagues compared fossilized coral samples from the Great Barrier Formation in Australia to modern coral structures. Using chemical composition analysis, the researchers found that coral fossils dating to about 15 million years ago (mya) most strongly resemble modern corals found in shallow, nutrient-poor waters typical of tropical environments. By contrast, they found that coral fossils dating to about 12 mya and 10 mya have a chemical signature that is similar to that of modern corals found in deeper, nutrient-rich waters typical of temperate zones. Ezeh's team therefore concluded that ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: temperate conditions replaced tropical environments as the most common ocean climate by about 15 mya.
choices.B: the majority of the coral fossils in the Great Barrier Formation developed under temperate conditions.
choices.C: temperate-zone conditions began occurring in some reef locations no later than 12 mya.
choices.D: the coral fossils in the Great Barrier Formation are of a more recent origin than scientists previously thought.

explanation: Choice C is the best answer because it presents the conclusion that most logically follows from the text's discussion of coral reef development over time. The text explains that Ezeh's team found coral fossils dating to 12 mya and 10 mya were similar to modern corals found in temperate zones. Because researchers found evidence of temperate-zone coral characteristics at 12 mya, it's reasonable to infer that temperate-zone conditions must have begun occurring in the Great Barrier Formation by this time.
